name: Estimating True Per-Window Costs for LA County Replacement Projects

mainEntity.name: How can homeowners in Los Angeles County calculate an approximate per-window price range that includes permits, stucco repair, and mid-grade energy-efficient glass?
mainEntity.text: How can homeowners in Los Angeles County calculate an approximate per-window price range that includes permits, stucco repair, and mid-grade energy-efficient glass?

acceptedAnswer.text: Advertised “per-window” prices in Los Angeles County often ignore typical add-ons, so homeowners benefit from building their own rough estimate. Begin by collecting several quotes for similar projects and identifying the base labor and product cost for a standard-sized, operable window with low‑E dual-pane glass from a reputable manufacturer. Next, factor in custom sizing, which is common in older homes and multi-family buildings, and may increase unit costs. Add approximate permit fees for your city—these can be a fixed amount or a percentage of project value—and allocate that across the total number of windows. Stucco or siding repair, plus interior trim or paint touch-ups, can significantly affect the true cost, especially for full-frame replacements. Ask contractors for typical per-opening repair allowances and include them in your calculation. After including disposal fees and a reasonable allowance for unforeseen issues on a handful of openings, divide the total estimated project cost by the number of windows. This average will almost always be higher than simple advertised installation rates but closer to what you will actually pay in Los Angeles County for mid-grade, energy-efficient replacement windows.
acceptedAnswer.description: Homeowners can estimate a realistic per-window price by starting with local base installation rates, then adding average costs for permits, custom sizing, stucco or trim repair, and low‑E dual-pane glass. Dividing the total project estimate by window count yields a more accurate per-opening figure than advertised base prices.
